lesson.title: The Lead That Makes You Smaller
lesson.hook: You get ahead, start playing safe, and your ball lands shorter, which hands them the court.
lesson.memHTML: Keep the depth that built the lead.
lesson.tomorrow: Next time you lead, watch where your ball is landing, not the scoreboard.

pro.label: Federer closing out Nadal, Wimbledon 2019
pro.moment: Federer needed five match points to finish the semi-final. Afterwards: "I was able to stick to my game plan, stay aggressive, stay offensive."
pro.read: Keep the game that built the lead.

drill.name: Start at 4-2
drill.how: Play sets starting at 4-2. The leader must land every rally ball past the service line. A short ball from the leader loses the point.

steps.name: Leading 5–2
steps.sit: You lead 5–2. Your rally ball has started landing shorter.
steps.q: What keeps the lead working for you?
opts: Keep it short, it's going in
Go for the line to finish
Float it safely down the middle
steps.payoff: Depth built the lead. Keep it.
steps.principle: Playing safe shouldn't mean playing shorter.
steps.why: Up 5–2, it's natural to take pace off and aim safer, and the ball lands shorter. A deep crosscourt is just as safe and keeps them back.
steps.take: Leading? Keep the depth that built the lead — margin, not a shorter ball.

lines.A: Deep crosscourt pushes them back — you're in time again.
lines.B: Shorter again: they step in — you're stretched.
lines.C: The line corner at pace — a fraction long.
lines.D: Short and soft — they step in and it's past you.

steps.name: They wait in your lane
steps.sit: Still ahead, but now they're waiting in your crosscourt lane before you hit.
steps.payoff: They moved, so you move the ball. Not because of the score.
steps.principle: Change direction because of the opponent, not the scoreboard.
steps.why: They're camped in your crosscourt lane, so the same ball feeds them. Down the line, well inside, makes them move.
steps.take: They're waiting in your lane? Change direction for them, not the score.

lines.A: Into the spot they're waiting in — you only just get there.
lines.B: Short into their lane — they step in; you're stretched.
lines.C: Down the line moves them across — you're in time.
lines.D: Closer to the crosscourt line — a fraction wide.

steps.name: 5–4, pushed back
steps.sit: At 5–4, a deep ball pushes you back. They're in the middle.
steps.q: What gives you a playable next ball?
opts: Drive it deep down the near line
Extra pace, deep to the far corner
steps.payoff: From deep, height and depth buy the time to recover.
steps.principle: Rebuilding the rally is still playing your game.
steps.why: This ball took your position, not your nerve. From way back, the line and extra pace miss too often; high and deep buys time.
steps.take: Pushed back at 5–4? Lift it deep through the middle and rebuild.

lines.A: From deep, the sideline asks too much — long.
lines.B: Short from deep, then forward — they step in and pass you.
lines.C: Extra pace from way back — wide.
lines.D: High and deep buys the time to get back.
